title: Runpad: micro-batch compass (personal tracker)
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal mini-sheet for micro-batch experiments. Use as a lightweight capture for runs I care about during deep-dive sessions. Keep it terse, timestamped, and action-driven.

Top-level notes / heuristics:
- Goal: find batch_size / quantization combos that meet 95th pct latency < 160ms for short-chunk requests (<=128 tokens) while minimizing token unit cost.
- Priorities: 95th latency -> cost -> quality. If quality regression > 2% BLEU-like metric, mark and revert.
- Always log model commit id and quant profile. If using KV cache prefixing, note cache hit rate.
- TODO: automate perf-to-cost conversion in dashboard (manual for now).

Run table (most recent first):
| run_id | date       | model_variant       | quant | batch | avg_lat_ms | p95_lat_ms | tks_per_s | cost_per_1k | kv_hit% | quality_delta | notes |
|--------|------------|---------------------|-------|-------|------------|-----------:|----------:|------------:|-------:|--------------:|-------|
| R-20250305-12 | 2025-03-05 | redwood-3b-v2       | 4-bit | 12    | 42         | 150        | 1,800     | $0.65      | 78%    | -0.8%         | baseline with cache; weird tail spikes @ p95 around 150ms when request size 120
| R-20250304-09 | 2025-03-04 | redwood-3b-v2       | 8-bit | 24    | 55         | 210        | 1,250     | $0.72      | 45%    | +0.2%         | higher batch reduces cost/sec but p95 violates SLO — KV cache not used for these runs
| R-20250227-03 | 2025-02-27 | opt-3b-tuned        | 4-bit | 8     | 38         | 135        | 2,100     | $0.59      | 82%    | -1.6%         | best perf so far for short tokens; slight quality drop on rare prompts (edge cases)
| R-20250220-01 | 2025-02-20 | redwood-3b-v1       | fp16  | 6     | 60         | 220        | 900       | $1.10      | 0%     | 0.0%          | legacy fp16 baseline (no quant), high cost; use as reference

Annotations and follow-ups:
- R-20250305-12: investigate p95 tail — look at batching alignment and async flush timing. Suspect one-off long pre-processing on worker when cache miss + disk swap. Add a run with pinned CPU affinity and disabled swap.
- R-20250304-09: try batch 16 instead of 24 with same 8-bit; hypothesize p95 will drop below 180ms and keep cost improvements.
- R-20250227-03: collect 1k samples of prompt classes that caused quality drop and run isolated eval to quantify regression. If >2% fail rate, revert quant profile.

Run commands / shorthand (copyable):
- baseline run: ./run_infer.sh --model redwood-3b-v2 --quant 4bit --batch 12 --cache-prefix on --commit $COMMIT
- quick smoke: ./run_infer.sh --model redwood-3b-v2 --quant 8bit --batch 16 --samples 200
- stress sweep: ./sweep.sh --model opt-3b-tuned --quant [4bit,8bit,fp16] --batch [6,8,12,16,24] --seed 42 --out ./sweeps/

Quick checklist before next session:
- [ ] Add automated p95 annotation in run collector (timestamp + trace id)
- [ ] Re-run R-20250305-12 with swap off and CPU pinning
- [ ] Run isolated quality eval for R-20250227-03 failing prompts
- [ ] Push promising config to canary with small traffic (5%) and monitor regressions

Notes to self (voice memo style):
- Keep this file minimal; move polished results to shared drive if I plan to show to team.
- If I find a combo that hits p95 <160ms and cost < $0.70 / k tokens with <1% quality regression, annotate as 'candidate' and open GH PR for tuning profiles.

End of sheet.
